title: Assups Neck
summary: Assups is recorded as a name applied to two necks of land in western Southampton town. The history represents the primary Assups Neck east of Quantuck Creek. The other form, Little Assups, belongs with the later Quiogue entry.
address_label: Neck east of Quantuck Creek, Quogue/Quiogue area, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate point on the neck east of Quantuck Creek based on Tooker's description; not a surveyed boundary or polygon.
why_this_matters: Assups Neck may preserve a Native personal name attached to a Southampton neck of land east of Quiogue. If the name comes from Assup, it shows how specific people and families could remain connected to local geography through the names recorded by others. Native Long Island history is not only about broad groups or territories, but also about named individuals, remembered places, and continuing community presence.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Assops, Assups, Assup, and Assoops. The name may come from Assup, a Native person whose name is compared with a Narragansett word for raccoon. The nearby Aspatuck creek form should not be treated as the same word.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names can tell us stories that would otherwise be unknown.”

— Nottinghamshire Historic Environment Record, What Can A Place Name Reveal About Its History? (2023), opening explanation
whereintheworld_content: Assups Neck preserves the relationship between Native personal names, meadow records, and the neck-and-creek geography of western Southampton. Keeping it distinct from Little Assups/Quiogue and Aspatuck Creek helps the map reflect the source geography more carefully.
